### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6a1d3a8d5fa1f1da7de3dbc2c9a9649867bf827` — the merge of head `df049c49b17e366f903f0423b849201055b97dc6` into base `819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6a1d3a8d5fa1f1da7de3dbc2c9a9649867bf827 && git checkout d6a1d3a8d5fa1f1da7de3dbc2c9a9649867bf827
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b df049c49b17e366f903f0423b849201055b97dc6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b && git merge --no-ff df049c49b17e366f903f0423b849201055b97dc6
```

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：`os skills install` / `update` 写到一半失败（磁盘满、权限、文件被占用）时，原来的技能和记录保持原样，再跑一次普通 `update` 就能恢复，不必加 `--force`。
- 为什么做：旧写法先删旧目录再写新的，中途失败会留下记录与目录对不上的状态。
- 出错会怎样：只动一条写盘路径；进程在毫秒级的改名阶段被强杀（含 Ctrl+C）仍可能留下混合状态，已要求另立小卡。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事，区域审完自己落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `b555879c64a6adbb5f267430d098c03beb0d2217` · 2026-11-19T12:19Z

- **形态** — draft, base `main`, 2 commits (red pin first, then the fix), 3 files, +239/−14. Merge-base `6d833b50`. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35495`: NOT governed, 253 lines ≤ 3000. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; CLI-only ⇒ no L2 owed. `Fixes #35079` is right: both "Done when" items are delivered.
- **Done when ① (stage, swap by rename, record after the swap)** — `applySkillsWrite`: all `underRoot` judgments and the manifest are computed before the first write (unchanged refusal-first property); new skills written under `<staging>/new`; each dropped and each touched skill renamed aside into `<staging>/old`, the staged copy renamed into place (rename-aside, since a directory cannot be renamed over a non-empty one); the record written in staging and renamed over `.objectstack-skills.json` last. Any throw ⇒ `undoSwap` reverses every recorded rename newest first, removes staging only when every undo succeeded, otherwise keeps it and appends where the copies are; then rethrows. Staging lives inside `dir` (same filesystem, so every swap step is a rename) and is hidden: `skillDirectories` filters `startsWith('.')` and `SKILL_NAME` needs a leading letter or digit, so no plan, `status` or catalog name can collide with it.
- **Done when ② (pin: failure injected mid-write; old skills and record usable; plain `update` recovers)** — proven, at the three points that matter: a staged file write (before any rename), the second skill's rename into place (after the first skill has been swapped, so the undo path is exercised), and the record's rename (after every skill is in place). Each arm asserts exit 1, the fault fired exactly once, `ENOSPC` printed, then every V1 byte, record `version`, `status --version V1 --check --json` exit 0 with `missing`/`modified`/`extra` empty and `mismatch: false`, nothing hidden beside the record; then a plain `update --version V2` (no `--force`) lands V2 with no leftover. A fourth case pins a killed run's leftover staging as invisible to `status` and removed by the next write. Red before the fix 4/34 on `060bd8fc` (the rename arm red as "fault never fired", i.e. the old code had no rename to fail), ablation back to base 4/34, restored blob == HEAD `36b9524f`. The `node:fs` fault seam is a hoisted pass-through mock in the shared harness, unarmed everywhere else; no production seam.
- **Changeset** — `@objectstack/cli` patch (published), read sentence by sentence: the old remove-then-write order and its `--force` consequence; hidden staging inside the skills directory; rename aside then into place; record renamed last; "any failure undoes the renames already done and is reported"; leftover hidden, never read, removed by the next write — all match the code. nit: "so the catalog is either wholly the old one or wholly the new one" holds for every failure the process survives to report, not for a hard kill mid-swap; if the body is edited anyway, "a failure it survives" would make that exact (optional; a changeset edit moves the head and needs an L1 delta).
- **门禁** — 53 check-runs on this head: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`.
- **Before landing (body only, no head move, no new L1)** — the 维护者速读 repeats two bullets verbatim (`风险与回滚` and `先看` each appear twice); dedupe them in the PR body.
- **范围外去向** — the residual hard-kill window in the swap phase (Acceptance notes, `carrier: none`): **a card is owed.** It is a real, user-reachable state, since Node's default SIGINT (Ctrl+C) also exits without running the `catch`, and the recovery is the same `--force` this card removes for thrown failures. The next write's `removeStagingLeftovers` also deletes the `old/` copies such a kill strands. The fix (a journal read and replayed before the plan, in `runSkillsWrite`, `skills-command.ts`) is outside this card's file surface, so it is not a REWORK reason. b1-B files it through `issue-create.mjs` under the filing gate: p3, `domain:cli`, dedupe words `skills, staging, swap, SIGKILL, SIGINT, journal, --force`, citing this PR's Acceptance notes and os-dev-report 7008338749.
- **落地条款** — not governed: b1-B lands this head after the body dedupe above. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
